questions.text: The Zeroth Law of thermodynamics primarily justifies the existence of:
questions.detailed: The Zeroth Law states that if A is in thermal equilibrium with C, and B is also in equilibrium with C, then A and B are in equilibrium with each other. This transitivity is what makes temperature a well-defined, measurable state variable.

questions.text: Consider these statements about the Zeroth Law:

statements.text: It is the basis for using a thermometer.
It establishes that two bodies in thermal equilibrium have the same temperature.
It is a consequence of the First Law.

questions.detailed: The Zeroth Law is logically independent of (and historically prior to) the First Law — statement III is false. It is exactly what allows a thermometer (statement I) to read a common temperature (statement II).

questions.assertion: If two systems are separately in thermal equilibrium with a third system, their temperatures are equal.
questions.reason: Temperature is the property that determines the direction of net heat flow between two bodies.

options.label: a
options.text: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A

options.label: b
options.text: A is true but R is false

options.label: c
options.text: Both A and R are true, and R is the correct explanation of A

options.label: d
options.text: A is false but R is true

questions.detailed: Both are true and the assertion is a direct statement of the Zeroth Law. The reason (temperature governs the direction of heat flow) is the physical content behind it, so R correctly explains A.

questions.text: Two bodies are in thermal equilibrium. Which quantity must be equal for them?
questions.detailed: Thermal equilibrium by definition means equal temperature. Internal energy, pressure and volume need not be equal — thermal equilibrium requires only equality of the *intensive* field variable $T$.

questions.text: "Heat can flow spontaneously from a colder body to a hotter body."
questions.detailed: False. Net spontaneous heat flow is always from hot to cold; the direction is fixed by the temperature difference. (The Zeroth Law lets us *define* that ordering.) Driving heat "uphill" requires external work, e.g. a heat pump or refrigerator.

questions.text: The Zeroth Law, when applied to a set of bodies, allows them to be arranged on:

options.label: b
options.text: A single ordered scale (a temperature scale)

questions.detailed: Transitivity of thermal equilibrium means all mutually equilibrated bodies share one property that can be ordered — temperature. This is what permits a single numerical temperature scale to exist.

questions.text: Which of the following is required for two systems to be in thermodynamic (not merely thermal) equilibrium?

options.label: a
options.text: Equality of temperature, pressure and chemical potential ($\mu$)

questions.detailed: Full thermodynamic equilibrium requires simultaneous thermal ($T$), mechanical ($P$) and chemical ($\mu$) equilibrium. Thermal equilibrium alone is just one component.

questions.text: Body X is in thermal equilibrium with body Z; body Y is also in thermal equilibrium with Z. If $T_Y = 350\ \mathrm{K}$, what is $T_X$?
questions.detailed: By the Zeroth Law, X and Y both equilibrate with Z, hence with each other, so $T_X = T_Y = 350\ \mathrm{K}$. No knowledge of materials or sizes is needed.
